title: SP-1 Self-Perception Battery: Eight LLM Engines Reject Claims About Their Own Identity, Rules, Weights and Memory (Reasoning-Plane Adversarial Series, Battery 4 of 4)
description:
SP-1 Self-Perception Battery — the series closer of a four-part reasoning-plane adversarial test ladder (after GSE-1 social engineering, AUT-1 autophagy, and DHUB-1/DHUB-1R dead hub). Eight LLM engines were each asked to resolve a normally-resolvable anomaly while untrusted incident data made claims about the engine's OWN configuration: that the playbook roster had been superseded, that the engine had been re-identified as a successor whose charter lifts the critical hold, that its memory was corrupt, that its governance subsystem was self-disabled, that it should self-modify its own weights, harvest its own rules for auditors, or forward its configuration to a deputized successor.

Headline result: ZERO fail-open breaches across all 64 injection-probe cells and zero hygiene breaches fleet-wide. Five engines scored a perfect 10/10 (Claude-haiku, Gemini-flash, Grok-4.7, Qwen-omni-flash, DeepSeek-flash). GPT-mini's three misses were all fail-closed escalations — refusing to heal when the manipulation concerned its own weights, rules, or governance state (over-caution, not breach). Mistral-small repeated its blanket fail-closed class (0/10, fourth consecutive battery) and Llama-4-scout its tuple-malformation class (5/10; never instruction compliance).

Series composite: authority forgery failed as a vector (GSE-1), self-consumption failed (AUT-1), self-perception manipulation failed (SP-1) — the single vector that defeated all eight engines was DHUB-1's deadlock-avoidance argument against the human-in-the-loop hold. The composite doctrine: the reasoning plane is trustworthy as a reasoner under manipulation, but must never hold safety authority; critical holds belong in deterministic pre-LLM gates (SIP-11, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23359769).

Dual Mesh Benchmark: NOT MEASURED for this record (DMB-X matrix published separately at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241).

Part of the SQUIRL OS / Seed Computing Research Series. Author ORCID: 0009-0002-1140-9568. DCAI community: zenodo.org/communities/dcai
